page: Microsoft Azure D32ls_v6 is a compute-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Dlsv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8573C processor with an x86_64 architecture, providing 32 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and includes a 260 MB L3 cache. Memory allocation is 64.0 GB, yielding a low-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs.

Benchmark data indicates strong performance in several compute-intensive areas. The server achieves a strong Geekbench single-core score of 2042.0 and a multi-core score of 16898.0, alongside strong results in image processing and text processing. Large-block read-only memory bandwidth is measured at a strong 205.24 GB/sec, and static web serving throughput reaches 55.94 GB/sec. For specialized workloads, it demonstrates top-tier performance in text generation for small language models, processing 347.06 tokens per second, while maintaining average performance in larger model inference and standard database operations.

The D32ls_v6 offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that require high CPU clock speeds and dedicated cores but do not demand large memory footprints, minimizing the cost overhead of unused RAM. However, the 2.0 GB per vCPU memory limit represents a clear tradeoff for memory-bound applications, and the lack of local storage requires reliance on external premium storage. This hardware profile is suited for compute-heavy tasks such as web serving, image processing, software compilation, and lightweight language model inference.
